key_insight: Global, guideline-based evaluation showed that many post-hoc XAI methods can look plausible on single ECGs while systematically missing the clinically important regions they are supposed to explain.
clinical_relevance: For ECG decision support, explanation methods should be judged against cardiology guidelines, because unreliable saliency maps could hide disease-relevant signal use and mislead clinicians.
method: Evaluated 13 gradient-based XAI methods on 4 binary ECG classifiers trained on PTB-XL.
Aggregated heartbeat-level explanations into global scores aligned with guideline-defined regions of interest.
Compared methods across two pattern types: low-amplitude segments and high-amplitude QRS morphology.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s evaluation, explanations often tracked signal amplitude rather than clinical relevance, with mean Spearman correlations up to 0.69 and nine of 13 methods falling below chance for at least one condition.
watch_item: Guideline-grounded evaluation improves oversight, but it depends on well-defined region labels and may not fully capture every clinically meaningful explanation pattern.
paper_title: Beyond Local Inspection: Global, Guideline-Grounded Evaluation of Post-hoc XAI Methods for ECG Classification
